properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-10-24, choosing the recommendations of the root cause walked on the Shop sample trial's lines of reasoning (hub fact:shop-sample-trial-friction-2026-10-24, items A1 and B9), relayed by the hub session: (1) "Premise says which": each premise states what it rests on, the owner's INTENT or its DELIVERY; and (2) "Intent" as the default: an unmarked premise of a step that concludes a DECISION reads as intent; everything else keeps today's delivery default. Proofs, arguments and verification arguments must read exactly as before.

WHAT IT MEANS:
- A requirement record carries two propositions: "X is required", true once its owner accepts it, and "X holds in the system", true once it is delivered. A design choice rests on the first; an assurance argument or a go/no-go decision rests on the second.
- INTENT: a Requirement, Capability or Interface reads by its owner's acceptance: accepted holds, proposed unknown, dropped or rejected fails.
- DELIVERY: today's reading: a requirement delivered by the roll-up or met, a capability realized and checked.
- The marker is a field on the premise link (PREMISE_OF), beside `role: assumed`, written per premise by add_inference.
- Unmarked, a premise of a step that concludes a Decision reads as intent; every other step reads delivery, as before. A decision that rests on delivery (a release, a go/no-go) marks those premises `delivery`.

OPTIONS CONSIDERED, ranked by correctness and root cause:
(1) the premise says which: CHOSEN.
(2) phase-named readings, a design reading and a build reading for every chain (the closure shape of 2026-09-29): not chosen. A choice's build reading means nothing, since delivery does not make a choice better justified, and it doubles every verdict.
(3) change the requirement reading everywhere so an accepted requirement holds: not chosen. An assurance argument would read "meets X" before anything is built, and capabilities and interfaces would stay as they were.
(4) keep the reading and fix only the guidance: not chosen. A design-time choice resting on intent could never read supported.
Default: (i) intent for a step concluding a Decision: CHOSEN; (ii) unmarked stays delivery everywhere: not chosen.

IT REVISES item 1 of req:a-choice-that-rests-on-checkable-premises-is-recorded-as-a-chain (2026-10-16), which named "a met requirement" as a checkable premise of a choice: an accepted requirement, read as its owner's intent, is one now.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-24: a premise says whether it rests on its owner's INTENT or on its DELIVERY; unmarked, a premise of a step that concludes a Decision reads as intent, and every other step keeps delivery
properties.rationale: The Shop sample trial (2026-10-24, flo2.io 671a764fa790c030) recorded 19 design choices, each with one step whose premises were the requirements, constraints, findings and decisions it rests on. Every chain read unknown, loop_status listed all 19 as having lost their reason, and detect_gaps raised 19 conclusions that do not follow, because a requirement premise read only its delivery. The root cause, walked as the skill, is the class recorded on 2026-09-29 for closure: a verdict defined for one purpose (delivery) reused for another (a design choice's grounds) because it was the only computation there was.
